1  AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 12.11.2014  PASSED IN MVC NO.6740/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE JUDGE,
 COURT OF SMALL CAUSE AND 26 TH ACMM, (SCCH-09),
 BANGALORE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:32703  MFA No. 894 of 2015 COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL

, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 12.11.2014 passed in M.V.C.No.6740/2012 by the Judge, Court of Small Causes and XXVI ACMM (SCCH-09), Bengaluru ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.text: Court of Small Causes and XXVI ACMM (SCCH-09), Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 05.08.2012 at about 10.00 a.m. while the petitioner was going in his Hero Honda bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EX/6257, opposite Adarsha Film Institute near Shashidhar Estate, on Hesaraghatta road, Bengaluru, a Hyundai Car bearing Reg.No.KA.05/MJ-6551, dashed against NC: 2024:KHC:32703 the motor cycle.
Due to which, he fell down and sustained injuries.
After taking treatment at Prestine Hospital, Rajajinagar and Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing on both the sides, allowed the claim petition granting compensation of Rs.1,81,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Prasad P., learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri.S.V.Hegde Mulkhand, learned counsel for the insurance company.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was a Senior Technician-Cum-Operator in International Airport, Bengaluru and was getting salary of Rs.26,737/-
per month at the time of accident.

He was laid to rest for 6 NC: 2024:KHC:32703 months, the estimate for removal of implants towards future medical expenses was Rs.40,000/-, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and sought for enhancement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company has contended that the petitioner was inpatient only for 4 days.
The petitioner has suffered fracture of right ankle and fracture of left tibia and fibula.

Though the doctor has assessed 20% whole body disability, the petitioner is resumed his work and drawing triple the quantum of salary now than he was getting earlier and injury is not effecting his future prospects.
The Tribunal has rightly considered all these aspects and assessed just compensation and it is not a case for enhancement and has supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
The insurance company has satisfied the award of the Tribunal.
Hence, there is no need to much discuss on the accident aspect.

The Tribunal has assessed a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.26,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.2,000/- towards incidental expenses,
Rs.78,000/- towards loss of income during laid up, Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.
9.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner being a supporting staff of International Airport, having sustained closed fracture of 1/3rd left tibia and fibula and closed fracture of lateral melleous right ankle, it certainly affect him in future.

The medical evidence even if it is accepted that petitioner has suffered 20% whole body disability, it could only be considered towards loss of amenities and discomfort as the petitioner is drawing more salary NC: 2024:KHC:32703 now than the salary that he was drawing at the time of accident.
10. Though the petitioner claims that he was laid up for 6 months, no evidence is placed.
But the learned counsel for the petitioner relying on the salary certificates for the months of May-2013 and June - 2014 to claim that the petitioner was laid up from 05.08.2012 to April 2013.
On perusal of the said pay slips, it is pertinent to note that the salary paid was for the period of 01.05.2013 to 31.05.2013, there is no reference for non-payment of salary prior to it.
The petitioner has not produced any Bank statement to show that he has not received any salary between 05.08.2012 upto April 2013.
Hence, the probabilities of the treatment resulting the petitioner to resume his work could be taken for a period of 4 months in the absence of evidence.
If the petitioner was applied for leave and not received any salary, nothing prevented him from producing the leave certificate issued by his NC: 2024:KHC:32703 employer.

The salary slip at Ex.P10 clearly shows that the petitioner was drawing the salary at Rs.26,737/- per month and for 4 months salary for laid up comes to Rs.1,06,948/-.
11.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering at Rs.40,000/-, towards medical expenses at Rs.26,000/- and towards future medical expenses at Rs.20,000/- are kept in intact.
The petitioner was under hospitalization for 4 days and he has attended follow up treatment and spent money towards traveling, food and nourishment and attendant charges.

Hence,
Rs.2,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side, it has to be compensated with Rs.15,000/-.

Towards loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.15,000/- is on lower side, it has to be taken at Manjunatha B vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182530318/
3 Rs.40,000/-.

entities.text: Manjunatha B vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,47,948/- as against Rs.1,81,000/-, thereby enhanced compensation of Rs.66,948/- rounded off to Rs.67,000/-.
It is the just NC: 2024:KHC:32703 compensation which the petitioner is entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.

Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified;

(iii) The petitioner would be entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.67,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit;
(iv) The insurance company is directed to deposit enhanced compensation with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE MKM Manjunatha B vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182530318/
